decisions.reason: Original Verification 2.1 inferred all F1 fields from observation maps and split sizes, although neither a loss nor an uncertainty diagnostic was supplied. This is an unsupported instantiation inference, hence a fatal logic defect. Added an explicit conditional empirical benchmark with squared loss, radius-ball coverage and its target, actual-list laws, and supplied method/budget/status records; preserved the complete physical Example.

Original Verification 2.1 asserted F1 instantiation without evaluation loss, uncertainty diagnostic, or compute/evaluation protocol. The cosine cutoff curates inputs and cannot supply reconstruction loss. This unsupported inference is a fatal logic defect. Added actual-list empirical laws, squared loss, ball-coverage diagnostic, supplied procedures and finite budgets, and explicit failure accounting without changing the fixed-incident-field Example.

Original Verification 2.1 inferred F1 population fields from sample counts and solver settings. Counts determine neither joint test atoms nor fitting/validation laws, loss, uncertainty diagnostic or comparison budgets. This invalid inference is a fatal logic defect. Added specified conditional empirical laws with y_i=F(i), squared loss, ball coverage, and supplied method/compute/status records; all original physical settings remain intact.

Original Verification 2.1 treated unspecified raw noise as the probability kernel required by F1. A raw-noise label supplies no such law, so the claimed instantiation was a fatal logic error. Added K(.|i)=delta_y_i on supplied labelled raw-data cases, with the corresponding conditional residual law, empirical fitting/validation/test laws and explicit evaluation protocol. This is conditional replay, not an invented physical acquisition law.

reviews.reason: Checked Fourier visibility, oriented triangle conjugations, ordered quadrangle ratio and nonzero domains against paper B.3 and pinned blackhole.py 110–140, 208–260. In the repair, finite labelled truths give measurable maps and a Dirac replay kernel; Euclidean squared loss and ball membership are product-measurable, and empirical integrals equal the stated averages. Coverage is a constructed diagnostic, not a claim of source-reported calibration.

Checked the finite sum is real-linear in physical real contrast and agrees with conjugation in pinned inverse_scatter.py 326–445; retained the paper/code distinction in Appendix B.1. The added finite-data laws are specified rather than inferred from counts. Dirac kernels on labelled cases and measurable squared loss/coverage satisfy F1 conditionally on the supplied procedures and budget records; Gaussian acquisition noise is not identified with conditional data replay.

Checked acoustic setup against paper B.4 and default zero wavefield construction through acoustic.py 61–86, Devito wavesolver.py 103–106 and dense.py 84–155. For supplied admissible discrete cases, K=delta_F is noise-free and measurable on finite truths. Empirical laws, squared loss, ball coverage and budget/status inputs establish the conditional benchmark. No continuum existence, solver convergence or generalization assertion is inferred.

On finite labelled truths the replay kernel is explicitly probability-valued and measurable; variable coil shapes use a finite disjoint union of Borel spaces. Squared loss and radius-ball coverage for real magnitude targets are measurable and have the stated empirical aggregates. The original raw-noise caveat and PSNR/SSIM/data-misfit reports remain intact.

repair_notes.construction: A1/A2 give a parameterized conditional finite-data specialization, not a reconstruction of the paper's full experimental protocol. Actual lists, complete candidate procedures and their numerical budget/metadata records are supplied inputs; no unavailable black-hole training data or executed benchmark result is claimed. X=U=C is a finite labelled truth space; P_train is a point mass at the complete fixed fitting record, and validation/test laws are explicit uniform atomic laws. The kernel replays recorded data; FWI additionally requires y_i=F(i). The loss is squared Euclidean error and the diagnostic is coverage of fixed-radius balls. Budget failures retain zero-image fallback outputs and visible statuses in both averages. This supplies missing fields while preserving source scope rather than withdrawing the benchmark instantiation claim.
